title: Program configurations satisfy the precondition
statement: For any natural numbers $a,b,f$, Boolean mode $m$, oracle $o$ on five indices and finite Boolean strings, finite Boolean string $y$, and abstract configuration $c$ with fifteen natural-number registers, $c$ satisfies the program precondition. Thus, when its instruction compares two registers, their indices are distinct; when it compares a register with the input payload, $y$ is a valid plain encoding; when it compares a register with either component of a paired payload, $y$ is a valid paired encoding; and when it calls an oracle, its argument registers are pairwise distinct.
hypotheses_covered: $o$ is an oracle on five indices and finite Boolean strings
$c$ is an abstract configuration with fifteen natural-number registers
replaced:
For every choice of natural numbers $a,b,f$, Boolean mode $m$, oracle $o$, bit string
$y$, and program configuration $c$, the configuration satisfies the program precondition
for the specified register program. In particular, if its current instruction compares
two registers, they are distinct; if it compares a register with the input payload, the
input is a valid plain encoding; if it compares with either component of a paired
payload, the input is a valid paired encoding; and if it calls an oracle, its argument
registers are pairwise distinct.
